description:
Short title
EM 'AI' excel

What should the AI do?
our so called EM 'AI' is really an excel workbook with macros. it takes the settle plate and contact plate counts, compares them to the alert and action limits for each room grade and emails the micro supervisor when something is over. we want to roll it out to all sites

Where will it be used?
QC laboratory

Does the AI output directly affect a batch, a GMP record, a QC result, a release or a process setting?
No, only indirectly

What kind of AI is it?
Rules or automation (not learning). excel macros

What happens with the output?
Information only: our own staff then do the task themselves. e-mail to the micro supervisor

Who checks the output, and how?
micro team still reviews every plate result as before

What data goes into it?
Confidential company data

Who provides it?
Built in-house

grid.note: Simplified grid inspired by the GAMP AI adaptiveness × autonomy concept; levels defined in this project.

decision.label: Not ML: proceed as a standard GMP system (Annex 11)
decision.explanation: The logic is explicitly programmed rather than learned from data, so it is not an AI/ML model in the sense of Annex 22 §1. It is a computerised system under Annex 11. If a vendor markets it as AI, ask for evidence of how it works (Annex 22 §2.2).

citations.quote: The document applies to machine learning (AI/ML) models which have obtained their functionality through training with data, rather than being explicitly programmed.
This annex applies to all forms of computerised systems used as part of a GMP regulated activities.

judgments.label: GMP, non-critical
judgments.rationale: Keyword baseline: the use is in a GMP setting ('ticked: No, only indirectly') but the output supports people rather than deciding.

citations.quote: If used in non-critical GMP applications, which do not have direct impact on patient safety, product quality or data integrity, personnel with adequate qualification and training should always be responsible for ensuring that the outputs from such models are suitable for the intended use, i.e. a human-in-the-loop…

judgments.label: Not ML (programmed logic)
judgments.rationale: Keyword baseline: the logic is configured or programmed rather than learned ('ticked: Rules or automation (not learning)').

citations.quote: The document applies to machine learning (AI/ML) models which have obtained their functionality through training with data, rather than being explicitly programmed.

judgments.label: AI informs, human decides
judgments.rationale: Keyword baseline: the tool provides information and people decide ('ticked: Information only: our own staff then do the task themselves').

citations.quote: Where a model is used to give an input to a decision made by a human operator (human-in-the-loop), and where the effort to test such model has been diminished, the description of the intended use should include the responsibility of the operator.

controls.title: Documented quality risk assessment
controls.what: A justified, documented risk assessment sets the extent of validation and data-integrity controls; formality proportional to risk.
controls.why: Source: Annex 11 (2011) §1 Risk Management; ICH Q9(R1) §4.3 Risk Assessment; ICH Q9(R1) §5.1 Formality in Quality Risk Management

citations.quote: As part of a risk management system, decisions on the extent of validation and data integrity controls should be based on a justified and documented risk assessment of the computerised system.
Risk assessment consists of the identification of hazards and the analysis and evaluation of risks associated with exposure to those hazards (as defined below).

citations.ref: ICH Q9(R1) §5.1 Formality in Quality Risk Management
citations.quote: The following may be characteristics of higher levels of formality: • All parts of the quality risk management process (risk assessment, risk control, risk review and risk communication) are explicitly performed, and stand-alone quality risk management reports or related documents which address all aspects of the…

controls.title: Computerised system validation
controls.what: Validate the application and qualify the infrastructure, scaled to risk; keep it in a validated state through its lifecycle.
controls.why: Source: Annex 11 (2011) §4.1 Validation; Annex 11 (draft) §2.1 Lifecycle management; Annex 11 (draft) §9.2 Quality risk management

citations.quote: Manufacturers should be able to justify their standards, protocols, acceptance criteria, procedures and records based on their risk assessment.
Computerised systems should be validated before use and maintained in a validated state throughout their lifecycle.
Computerised systems should be qualified and validated in accordance with the principles of quality risk management.

controls.title: Data integrity (ALCOA+)
controls.what: Data the system captures, processes or reports must be trustworthy (ALCOA+); assess data criticality with QRM; the regulated user stays accountable for records produced with AI.
controls.why: Source: Annex 11 (draft) §2.4 Data integrity; Annex 11 (draft) §4.5 Data integrity; Chapter 4 (draft) §4.24 General Requirements For Documentation

citations.quote: It is critically important that data captured, analysed and reported by systems used in GMP activities are trustworthy.

Quality risk management principles should be used to assess the criticality of data to product quality, patient safety and data integrity, the vulnerability of data to deliberate or indeliberate alteration, deletion or loss, and the likelihood of detection of such actions.

The accountability for the integrity of documents, records or (raw) data produced or processed with artificial intelligence or any other automatic means (e.g. validation scripts) rests with the regulated user.

controls.title: Audit trail
controls.what: Record GMP-relevant user interactions: creation, change and deletion of data with user, time and reason (Annex 11). This tool's recommendation for AI systems: also log inputs, model and prompt versions and outputs.
controls.why: Source: Annex 11 (2011) §9 Audit Trails; Annex 11 (draft) §12.2 Who, what, when, why

citations.quote: For change or deletion of GMP-relevant data the reason should be documented.
Where data is changed from an old value to a new value, systems should automatically prompt the user for, and register the reason, why the change was made.

controls.title: Change and configuration management
controls.what: Changes to the system (including model, prompt or configuration) are made in a controlled manner under a defined procedure.
controls.why: Source: Annex 11 (2011) §10 Change and Configuration Management; Annex 11 (draft) §3.1 Pharmaceutical quality system

citations.quote: Any changes to a computerised system including system configurations should only be made in a controlled manner in accordance with a defined procedure.

Any change to a computerised system including but not limited to its configuration, its hardware and software components, and its platform and operating system, are made in a controlled manner and in accordance with defined procedures.

controls.title: Supplier and service-provider oversight
controls.what: Formal agreements, supplier audit and ongoing oversight; review supplier documentation for externally provided models. For hosted AI services, agree how new model versions are released and whether you can test them before release.
controls.why: Source: Annex 11 (2011) §3.1 Suppliers and Service Providers; Annex 22 (draft) §2.2 Documentation; Annex 11 (draft) §7.2 Audit; Annex 11 (draft) §7.5 Contracts

citations.quote: When third parties (e.g. suppliers, service providers) are used e.g. to provide, install, configure, integrate, validate, maintain (e.g. via remote access), modify or retain a computerised system or related service or for data processing, formal agreements must exist between the manufacturer and any third parties,…

Documentation for activities described in this section should be available and reviewed by the regulated user irrespective of whether a model is trained, validated and tested in-house or whether it is provided by a supplier or service provider.

When a regulated user is relying on a vendor’s or a service provider’s qualification and/or operation of a system used in GMP activities, the regulated user should, according to risk and system criticality, conduct an audit or a thorough assessment to determine the adequacy of the vendor or service provider’s…
Describes the activities and documentation to be provided ii.

controls.title: Periodic review
controls.what: Review the system periodically after go-live to verify it stays in a validated state and fit for its intended use.
controls.why: Source: Annex 11 (draft) §14.1 Periodic reviews; Annex 11 (2011) §11 Periodic evaluation

citations.quote: This review should verify whether the system remains 'fit for intended use' and in 'a validated state', or whether changes should be made and re-validation (complete or in parts) is required.
Computerised systems should be periodically evaluated to confirm that they remain in a valid state and are compliant with GMP.

controls.title: Roles, qualification and training
controls.what: Defined responsibilities and adequate training for everyone using or maintaining the system; AI literacy for staff using AI.
controls.why: Source: Annex 22 (draft) §2.1 Personnel; Annex 11 (draft) §5.2 Training; EU AI Act: Article 4: AI literacy

citations.quote: All personnel should have adequate qualifications, defined responsibilities and appropriate level of access.

All parties involved with computerised systems used in GMP activities should have adequate system specific training, and appropriate qualifications and experience, corresponding to their assigned responsibilities, duties and access privileges.

citations.ref: EU AI Act: Article 4: AI literacy
citations.quote: Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf, taking into account their technical knowledge, experience, education and training and the…

warnings: Draft Annex 22, the draft Annex 11 and the draft Chapter 4 are consultation drafts (July 2025). The final texts may differ.
